articles.title: Super League: Harvey Barron scores treble as Hull FC end losing run with win over St Helens
articles.summary: Harvey Barron scored a first senior treble as Hull FC ended a seven-game losing run with a comeback win at St Helens, who are still reeling from last month's exit of Paul Rowley after less than a year as head coach
articles.body:
Barron's treble boosted the Black and Whites' hopes of avoiding the Super League wooden spoon while casting further doubt on Saints making the end of season play-offs.

Hull had not previously won at the BrewDog Stadium in 10 games and nine years and sat just two points off bottom club Huddersfield Giants.

However, in this battle of the interim coaches, Andy Last got the better of counterpart Eamon O'Carroll, who last weekend oversaw Saints' first defeat at York in more than 80 years.

Hull trailed 14-10 approaching half-time but Barron struck almost on the hooter and completed his career landmark hat-trick after 47 minutes before substitute Cade Cust crashed over three minutes later.

Those 16 points in 11 minutes stunned Saints, still reeling from last month's exit of Paul Rowley after less than a year as head coach.

Despite a first away victory on Saints' territory since August 2017, Hull stay 13th although they are now level on points with Bradford Bulls.

St Helens have never failed to reach the play-offs but they remain seventh with all teams above them to play in the coming days.

They led three times in the opening 40 minutes but conceded their advantage each time and were fortunate to be level at 14-14.

The game's first mistake after barely two minutes saw full-back Logan Moy's knock-on punished by winger Lewis Murphy, who finished in the corner.

FC were behind only five minutes as Zak Hardaker's pass sent in Barron for the first of his treble.

Hastings edged Saints in front again with an 18th-minute penalty for Tom Briscoe's high tackle.

Prop Herman Ese'ese had a second Hull try ruled out for a double movement while he and Barron were repelled in quick succession before the visitors' deservedly hit the front.

Stand-off Jake Arthur's double cut-out pass freed Lewis Martin to finish in the left corner to make it 10-8.

Barron was denied again by last-gasp cover tackling and it was against the run of play when Jack Welsby raced 30 metres to touch down.

With 37 seconds remaining Saints captain Hastings dropped out. Thirty four seconds later Barron seized on Aidan Sezer's angled kick to cross again, waiting anxiously before video referee Chris Kendall overturned Liam Rush's on-field decision of 'no try'.

Tries for Barron and Cust, both converted by Hardaker, virtually put the contest out of reach.

By the time Harry Robertson scored a consolation try, Hardaker's 70th-minute penalty sealed the deal for Hull FC, who finished off with a further try from ex-Saint James Bell.

In the Women's Super League, Wigan Warriors saw off rivals St Helens 44-6 in the first match of the new Super Four format.

The defending champions outclassed St Helens with Ellise Derbyshire and Eva Hunter scoring a brace with further scores from Anna Davies, Molly Jones, Remi Wilton, Jenna Foubister and Mary Coleman at the BrewDog Stadium.

articles.title: Super League: Leeds Rhinos secure play-off spot with comeback win over Wakefield Trinity, Hull KR and Leigh Leopards pick up crucial victories
articles.summary: Leeds Rhinos are the first team to secure their play-off spot following a victory over Wakefield Trinity; Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live
articles.body:
​​​​​​Former Leeds half-back Jack Sinfield, son of Rhinos great Kevin, was outstanding against the club that released him at the end of last year, providing the assist for two of Wakefield's three tries in eight first-half minutes to put the hosts 16-0 ahead.

Sinfield then went over after half-time to put Wakefield 22-6 ahead and give Trinity hope of moving level on points with Leeds, but the league leaders impressively went up a gear in the final half hour.

James McDonnell and Cameron Smith struck with Sinfield off the pitch but even with the 21-year-old back on, the momentum was with Leeds and Hankinson sprung into action from a low kick from Jake Connor, who added his fourth conversion in the 78th minute to give his side the win.

Leeds are now four points clear of their West Yorkshire rivals at the top of the table after ending Wakefield's seven-match winning streak.

It was Leeds who started stronger as Wakefield were initially hemmed in early on, with three goal-line drop-outs following Connor's 40-20 but Sinfield was one of three defenders to drive returning Leeds captain Ash Handley into touch which released the building pressure.

Given the opportunity to break upfield themselves, Wakefield showed much more of a cutting edge as Sinfield's dink over the top bounced and spun cruelly past covering defender Lachie Miller, allowing Isaiah Vagana to open the scoring.

Powerful prop Caius Faatili made a near-instant impact from the bench, bulldozing through Leeds' defence before passing inside for Caleb Hamlin-Uele to go under the posts, while Sinfield's dummy and offload saw Jayden Myers dot down in the corner as Wakefield established a 16-0 lead after 29 minutes.

Sinfield blotted his copybook by missing his third conversion and Wakefield then switched off before half-time as Brodie Croft cruised through a yawning gap to get Leeds on the board.

Wakefield were quickest out of the traps after the break, Sinfield collecting a return pass from Faatili and feigning to go out wide before muscling through two defenders, with the try given by the video referee despite suspicions the ball had not been cleanly grounded.

Sinfield added the extras but then headed for the tunnel soon after and Leeds pounced. Although Alfie Edgell's foot was dragged into touch after touching down and Jarrod O'Connor was held up over the line, McDonnell made no mistake with half an hour to go.

Wakefield-bound Smith showed what his new side will be getting from next year by wriggling free of his future team-mates and exploiting a gap to score, with Jake Connor's third conversion bringing Leeds to within four points.

After Sinfield came back on, Cameron Scott had an opportunity to extend Wakefield's lead but his foot was clawed into touch before he got the ball down in the corner and from then on, it was one-way traffic from then on as Leeds came on strong in the final quarter.

Handley was denied a try following a high ball from Croft because of a knock-on but Leeds would not be denied as Hankinson dotted down following a clever grubber from Connor, who split the posts with his conversion kick to put the visitors ahead for the first time with three minutes left.

Hull KR inflicted more woe on Castleford with an eight-try thrashing of the crisis club in the Betfred Super League.

Castleford were without head coach Ryan Carr due to "personal reasons" for the clash at the OneBore Stadium, but entered the fixture after five defeats in six matches.

Any hope of an upturn in fortunes quickly went out the window with play-off chasing Rovers able to run in six second-half scores with Tom Davies and Tyrone May going over twice for a brace each in a 44-0 victory.

It took 12 minutes for the deadlock to be broken when Jez Litten latched on to his own grubber kick to jot down.

Davies added a second before the break, but Castleford were firmly in the contest at half-time with the score at 10-0.

However, May's 45th-minute effort opened the floodgates and sparked a spell of four tries in 11 minutes.

Joe Burgess grabbed another for Rovers before Peta Hiku went over, which was backed up by a second for May.

Davies completed his brace with 15 minutes left and Rhyse Martin rounded off the scoring in the 73rd minute to cap a fine 14-point individual display for the Papua New Guinea forward.

Leigh boost play-off hopes with win over York

Leigh Leopards provided a welcome boost to their play-off hopes with a 22-14 win over York Knights.

The Leopards had a slender 12-10 half-time lead thanks to tries from Josh Charnley and Joe Ofahengaue, Jon Bennison touching down twice for the Knights.

In the second half, Leigh seemingly took control again and with tries from Andy Badrock and David Armstrong, they stretched their lead to 22-10.

York did hit back once again as Bennison went over for his hat-trick with eight minutes left on the clock but it was not enough to stop Leigh picking up the victory.

Adrian Lam's side now sit on 28 points in sixth spot, four points ahead of St Helens in seventh.

articles.title: Huddersfield Giants moving to Dewsbury: Super League side switching home from 2027 season onwards
articles.summary: Huddersfield Giants' intention is to move into Dewsbury's Flair Stadium, subject to RFL board approval, investing a projected £10m-plus in developing the ground; the investment would include the construction of a new stand that will increase capacity from 5,000 to 8,000 fans
articles.body:
The Giants' intention is to move into Dewsbury's Flair Stadium, subject to RFL board approval, investing a projected £10m-plus in developing the ground.

The investment will deliver a transformational upgrade of the venue, including the construction of a new stand that will increase capacity from 5,000 to around 8,000 spectators, creating a viewing area on all four sides of the pitch.

The redevelopment will also feature refurbishment of the fan concourses, significant upgrades to existing and new hospitality suites, new bars and food areas, both male and female player dressing rooms, and press facilities elevating the stadium to Super League standards.

An agreement has been reached following extensive and amicable negotiations with Betfred Championship team, Dewsbury Rams, and a strong partnership between the two clubs has been forged. The Flair will continue to host the Rams in the newly-upgraded and dual-branded facility.

This comes following a period of uncertainty for the Giants after seeking a permanent location in the Huddersfield area.

Owner of the club, Ken Davy OBE, has explored several alternative sites, including The Shay Stadium in Halifax.

Speaking of the decision, Davy said: "It's no secret that as a club, we have fought to find a home in Huddersfield. We had to move from Fartown, from Leeds Road, and now from the Accu Stadium. But the Huddersfield Giants will not retreat. We will not compromise or quietly shuffle into the shadows.

"While we remain the Huddersfield Giants, I am proud to announce that our stage for the 2027 season and beyond is Dewsbury.

"The Flair Stadium is the perfect location for us, it will have the right capacity and facilities for the Giants and its fans to thrive while we continue the search for our permanent home. Our one giant future starts now.

"My overriding aim is to create a purpose-built stadium within Huddersfield for the Giants to call home. My commitment on that has not wavered. However, that was not feasible for the 2027 season."

Ralph Rimmer OBE, executive chairman of the Huddersfield Giants, added: "The Giants' future is bright, and we are excited to lead the club into this new era.

"For fans, the matchday experience will be our focus. A smaller, more intimate ground means the crowd is closer to the action, letting the atmosphere grow and support the team out on the pitch.

"The Flair Stadium offers everything that supporters need from parking and accessibility to corporate hospitality and function rooms.

"We can't wait to welcome you for the 2027 season and beyond to be a part of the Giant future we have in store."

Jackson: Dewsbury not yet Super Lsague ready

Huddersfield Giants non-executive director Rebecca Jackson:

"[Dewsbury flair stadium] is not quite Super League ready yet, so we definitely need to bring it up to standard.

"We'll be spending around £10m - a huge investment - to ensure that it can actually be the place where the Huddersfield Giants can play, and really have the atmosphere for both the fans and our partners - and that means building a new stand too, which is very exciting.

"This is just a medium-term plan. We are still looking to build our own stadium within Huddersfield, which has been something that we've worked on for a really long time.

"We've just unfortunately not been able to secure a site quite yet with the local authorities, but a lot of discussion has been happening.

"We're hoping that this is going to be able to be a bit of a stop gap for us - a medium-term solution - to then be able to get back into Huddersfield long term."

articles.title: Super League: Wigan thrash Toulouse to move second as Huddersfield win third straight match with victory over Catalans
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors move second with a win over Toulouse as Huddersfield Giants secure victory over Catalans Dragons; Warrington thrash Bradford; Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live
articles.body:
The Giants raced into an 18-point lead inside the opening 15 minutes through Halsall's double and Fenton Rogers before further tries from Wrench, Sam Hewitt and Zane Dunford put them 36-0 up at half-time.

Catalans rallied in the second half despite the dismissal of loose forward Franck Maria for a high tackle, with Ben Condon scoring twice and further efforts from Leo Darrelatour and Charlie Staines, while Wrench also added his second as Giants claimed the spoils.

Halsall raced 80 metres for an early interception try and prop Rogers barged over for Giants' second before Halsall dived over in the corner to put the home side in control.

Centre Wrench followed up winger Lewis Jagger's break to go over, Hewitt dotted down Tuimoala Lolohea's kick and Dunford crashed over for the Giants' sixth first-half try, with George Flanagan nailing all six conversions.

Catalans responded early in the second half when second row Condon burst over for Toby Sexton to convert, but another converted long-range interception try by Wrench restored Huddersfield's 36-point lead.

Maria was then sent off for the visitors in the 62nd minute for a high tackle on George King and although Catalans went over through Condon's try and efforts from Darrelatour and Staines, they were only consolations.

The Giants remain bottom of the table, but their third straight Super League win came after a club announcement at half-time in which they outlined plans to groundshare with Dewsbury at Flair Stadium next season.

Wigan move second with win over Toulouse

Wigan moved up to second as they overcame some first-half resistance from Toulouse before running away with it after the interval in a 48-18 win.

Zach Eckersley and Liam Marshall scored in both halves in an eight-try win for the Warriors, with Harry Smith boasting a 100 per cent conversion rate from the kicking tee at the Brick Community Stadium.

But Wigan, who moved to within two points of league leaders Leeds, did not have things all their own way, with their French visitors drawing level at 18-18 shortly before half-time.

Toulouse opened the scoring through Paul Ulberg stepping off the flank for a try but Eckersley touched down following a cut-out pass from Bevan French, who powered his way over soon after to put Wigan ahead.

Marshall then dotted down as Wigan looked to be moving up a gear but Romeo Tropis and Cesar Rouge struck either side of the half hour, with Rouge converting both to drag Toulouse level.

Wigan, though, went in at the break with a six-point lead when Noah Hodkinson went over in the right corner and from there, the home side did not look back.

Hodkinson turned provider at the start of the second half, passing back inside for Eckersley's second, while Sam Eseh crashed his way through several defenders to go over underneath the posts.

Jai Field raced on to French's chip over the top before Marshall's acrobatic finish and Smith's conversion made it 30 unanswered points as Wigan sealed an emphatic win to leapfrog Wakefield in the table.

Warrington dismantle Bradford to keep pressure on league leaders

Warrington scored seven tries to thrash Bradford 42-4 and stay in the race for a top-two finish in the Betfred Super League.

The fourth-placed Wolves are six points behind leaders Leeds and four points off Wigan in second with a game in hand.

Matty Ashton (2), Albert Hopoate, Toby King, Joe Philbin, Jordy Crowther and Ewan Irwin went over as second-from-bottom Bradford had their winless streak extended to nine games.

The 18-year-old Irwin converted every try and has now had 15 consecutive successful kicks at goals.

Despite Ethan Ryan striking an early blow for the Bulls with his 13th Super League try of the season, the result was never in doubt after Warrington established command halfway through the first period.

Ashton, Hopoate and King scored before the break and the flawless kicking of Irwin made it 18-4.

Bradford prop Jamie Gill had a try disallowed after Chris Atkin pulled back Danny Walker, further proof that it was not to be the Bulls' day.

Warrington did not take their foot off the gas as four more tries completed the rout, Irwin's the pick of the bunch after the teenager's twinkling footwork left the Bulls defence bemused.

articles.title: Tommy Makinson: Catalans Dragons wing and former St Helens try machine announces he will retire at end of 2026 campaign
articles.summary: Catalans Dragons wing Tommy Makinson announces he will retire at end of 2026 Super League season; Makinson turns 35 in October and won five Super League titles with St Helens during his career; Round 23 of Super League commences from Thursday August 13, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The Catalans Dragons wing, 34, spent the majority of his career with St Helens between 2011 and 2024, winning five Super League titles in 2014, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022 and making more than 300 appearances.

Makinson also won a World Club Challenge, a Challenge Cup and four League Leaders' Shields with Saints, and was selected in the Super League Dream Team on three occasions.

A prolific try scorer, Makinson scored over 200 tries for St Helens and has since notched 20 tries in 37 appearances for Catalans after joining the club ahead of the 2025 season. He also represented England over 20 times.

"As the 2026 season moves towards its final stages, I feel now is the right time to announce that this will be my final season as a professional rugby league player," Makinson posted on Instagram.

"Rugby league has been incredibly kind to me, and when I look back on the journey I've been on, I feel nothing but pride and gratitude. I've been very fortunate to live out a dream I had as a kid and represent some of the biggest clubs both in England and France and also the pinnacle which is representing my country.

"There have been so many highs, some difficult moments, incredible memories and friendships that will last a lifetime. I wouldn't have been able to experience any of it without the unbelievable support I've had from my family, friends, team-mates, coaches, staff, supporters and everyone who has played a part in my career. To each and every one of you, thank you.

"I've still got a few games left, and I want to enjoy every second of them. I'll be taking it all in, appreciating the moments and giving everything I have to finish this chapter of my career in the best possible way.

"It's hard to put into words what rugby league has given me, but I know how lucky I am to have lived this life and played the game I love for as long as I have."

articles.title: Mac Allister Scores Long-Range Screamer To Give Liverpool Win vs. Atletico Madrid
articles.summary: Mac Allister unleashed a ferocious strike from outside of the box as Liverpool came back from a goal down at Anfield.
articles.body: A day after revealing his disappointment over the lack of a new contract offer by Liverpool, Alexis Mac Allister delivered the perfect response with the winning goal in a 2-1 victory against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Wednesday. Mac Allister unleashed a ferocious strike from outside of the box as Liverpool came back from a goal down at Anfield. The Argentina international, who joined Liverpool in 2023, raced away to celebrate in front of the home fans. It was in stark contrast to his sombre tone ahead of the game when discussing the uncertainty over his position at the club. "I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract," he said during a pre-match news conference on Tuesday. Mac Allister's contract runs until 2028, so there is no urgency for Liverpool to renew yet. But his goal five minutes after after halftime was a reminder of his qualities, firing powerfully into the corner and beyond the reach of Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak. Atletico had taken the lead through Marcos Llorente after 17 minutes, with the midfielder extending his remarkable goal-scoring run at Anfield. It was his fifth goal in his last three visits to Merseyside, having famously scored twice as Atletico eliminated then-defending champion Liverpool from the tournament just before the Covid 19 lockdown in 2020. Dominik Szoboszlai leveled in the 40th before Mac Allister's winner. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: James Rodríguez y la coincidencia maldita del Avellino con los papas
articles.standfirst: El equipo al que llegaría James tiene una sincronía maldita con los papas
articles.summary: El equipo al que llegaría James tiene una sincronía maldita con los papas
articles.body: El fútbol está plagado de cábalas, supersticiones y casualidades que desafían la lógica. Sin embargo, la historia de la Unione Sportiva Avellino 1912, el modesto club del sur de Italia al que llegaría James Rodríguez, cruza la frontera entre el deporte y lo esotérico. Su peculiar fenómeno tiene a los aficionados al balompié y a los observadores del Vaticano atónitos: desde hace más de medio siglo, cada vez que el Avellino logra subir de categoría, un Papa fallece o renuncia a su pontificado. La inquietante coincidencia se remonta al año 1958. En aquel entonces, el club de la región de Campania logró el ascenso a la Serie C. Ese mismo año, el mundo lloraba la muerte de Pío XII. Lo que parecía un hecho puramente anecdótico terminó por convertirse en un patrón ininterrumpido a lo largo de las décadas: Con la muerte de Francisco en abril de 2025, el fenómeno sumó su séptimo episodio histórico. La vinculación entre el Santo Padre argentino y la institución irpina no era ajena; en su momento, el club le obsequió una camiseta oficial al pontífice en una audiencia, una imagen que la propia entidad volvió a homenajear tras la triste noticia. Lo cierto es que esta "sincronía maldita" ha colocado a la ciudad de Avellino en el foco internacional. Mientras sus aficionadas celebran los éxitos deportivos en el césped, en los pasillos de la liga italiana y en las redes sociales no se deja de comentar este insólito hilo invisible que conecta los logros del club verdebianco con los acontecimientos en la Santa Sede.

articles.title: Dodgers Reportedly Call Up Top Prospect Josue De Paula
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers are calling up top-rated prospect Josue De Paula from Double-A, according to multiple reports.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Dodgers are calling up top prospect Josue De Paula straight from Double-A, according to multiple reports on Wednesday. The Athletic was the first to report. De Paula is expected to get at-bats at designated hitter after Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced on Wednesday that Shohei Ohtani will be heading to the IL. De Paula, 21, is the No. 6 ranked prospect in baseball and the highest-rated outfielder. He spent the 2026 season with the Dodgers' Double-A minor league affiliate, the Tulsa Drillers, and hit 27 home runs in 588 plate appearances, while posting a slash line of .303/.401/.547. He also had stolen 31 games in 123 games. Prior to being signed by the Dodgers out of the Dominican Republic in 2022, he played out of El Niche Academy. He signed a $397,500 contract with the Dodgers in January 2022. De Paula was named the 2025 Futures Game MVP.

articles.title: Suiza instala en un lago 1.400 paneles solares encadenados a pesas en el fondo: durante seis meses se vacía de agua y se anclan en una plataforma
articles.standfirst: Un proyecto de la empresa Romande Energie y que sería algo único en el mundo
articles.summary: Un proyecto de la empresa Romande Energie y que sería algo único en el mundo
articles.body: Los paneles solares parece que son el futuro de la humanidad, en cuanto a energía limpia se trata, son múltiples los proyectos que juegan con esta idea y uno de ellos ha instalado 1.400 placas en el lago de una montaña, a unos 1.810 metros de altitud. Se trata de la compañía Romande Energie y ha elegido el lago des Toules, un embalse alpino en Suiza, en el cantón de Valais, para crear un parque solar experimental que pasa la mitad del año posado sobre tierra firme, y la otra mitad elevado sobre el agua. A diferencia de los lagos naturales, este embalse hidroeléctrico se drena en determinados momentos del año, generando un cambio en el nivel del agua de hasta 15 metros. Para solucionar este problema, los ingenieros optaron por una estructura flexible: una plataforma de aluminio y polietileno que soporta 1.400 paneles fotovoltaicos bifaciales, encadenada a pesas que se sujetan en el fondo del lugar. Cuando el nivel baja por completo, la instalación se posa sobre el material diseñado para amortiguar el impacto, una vez vuelve a subir el nivel del agua, se mantiene funcionando de forma flotante, pudiendo ser usado durante todo el año. articles.title: Raúl Varela: "Raphinha está a punto de convertirse en el mejor brasileño que ha pasado por el Barcelona"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu defiende el impacto del delantero y lo sitúa por encima de Dani Alves, Ronaldo, Ronaldinho, Rivaldo y Neymar
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu defiende el impacto del delantero y lo sitúa por encima de Dani Alves, Ronaldo, Ronaldinho, Rivaldo y Neymar
articles.body: Raphinha vuelve a estar en el centro de los elogios. Raúl Varela puso sobre la mesa en La Tribu el impacto que está teniendo el delantero brasileño en el Barcelona y fue un paso más allá al compararlo con algunos de los grandes nombres de su país que han vestido la camiseta azulgrana. "Al debate le faltan cuatro goles mal contados para abrirse", comenzó Varela antes de recordar el recorrido de Raphinha desde su llegada al club: "Ese jugador llamado Raphael Días está a punto de convertirse en el mejor brasileño que ha pasado por el vestuario del Camp Nou vistiendo la camiseta azulgrana". Una afirmación de peso teniendo en cuenta la nómina de brasileños que han dejado huella en el Barcelona. Varela puso varios nombres encima de la mesa: Dani Alves, Ronaldo, Ronaldinho, Rivaldo y Neymar. "Y mira que hay competencia", señaló antes de repasar a algunos de ellos: "Los más de cuarenta títulos con un impacto descomunal de Dani Alves desde el lateral derecho, por supuesto los goles y la magia, aunque excesivamente concentrada en el tiempo de Ronaldo el Fenómeno y Ronaldinho, que duró tres telediarios en la élite. Me acuerdo de Rivaldo que fue totalmente determinante cuando se lo arrebataron al Depor y, claro está, Neymar que llegó a jugar, al menos, una temporada al nivel del mismísimo Leo Messi". Varela considera que muchos de esos futbolistas tenían mayores cualidades técnicas, carisma y repercusión mediática que Raphinha, pero eso no impide que el actual jugador azulgrana se haya convertido en una pieza fundamental: "Todos ellos jugadores imponentes, de mayores cualidades técnicas que el actual delantero de Flick, también con más carisma y foco mediático de este hombre de perfil bajo que sabe convivir a la sombra que proyecta Lamine". El director de La Tribu puso también el foco en los números y en todo aquello que aporta Raphinha más allá de los goles: "83 goles ya de culé y un montón de intangibles que le convierten en indiscutible, en líder y en capitán de un equipo que ha arrancado de forma sencillamente perfecta la temporada". Para Varela, el brasileño pertenece a esa clase de futbolistas que quizá no acaparan tanto foco fuera del terreno de juego, pero que resultan fundamentales para sus entrenadores: "Raphinha es uno de tantos de esa estirpe que no vende tantas camisetas como otros, ni firma tantos autógrafos. Pero a la hora de la verdad siempre encuentra acomodo en el once de su equipo sea en el puesto que sea porque tanto te fríe una corbata como te plancha un huevo". Y cerró su reflexión con una reivindicación contundente del brasileño: "Jugador apreciado y valorado por los de dentro, merece mayor reconocimiento fuera. Este Barça vuela porque el que bate las alas se llama Raphinha".

articles.title: Beaten by bias? Karnataka’s Krishik M misses Asian Games bus despite meeting AFI benchmark thrice
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: BENGALURU: They say truth is stranger than fiction — a lesson Karnataka’s top hurdler has just been handed the hard way.Despite clearing Athletics Fed.
articles.body: BENGALURU: They say truth is stranger than fiction — a lesson Karnataka’s top hurdler has just been handed the hard way.Despite clearing Athletics Federation of India’s (AFI) Asian Games qualifying benchmark not once but thrice, Krishik M still finds himself left out of the 110-metre men’s hurdles squad for the upcoming continental showpiece in Japan.The omission comes as a bitter blow to the 22-year-old BTech graduate — and to his father, Manjunatha, who gave up his job to support Krishik and his brother Kanishk in their pursuit of athletic careers.The AFI selection committee defended its decision pointing to the Inter-State meet in Bhubaneswar, where Krishik finished third – missing out on the federation's cutoff of a top-two finish.However, sources point towards a double standard, noting that the committee showed leniency to seasoned campaigners Tajinderpal Singh Toor (men’s shot put) and Annu Rani (women’s javelin throw) despite similar qualifying setbacks.Worse still, even after Tejas Shirse — the sole athlete initially picked for the men's 110-metre hurdles — withdrew from the Asian Games squad with an injury, the federation still didn’t call up Krishik.Krishik’s exclusion stands in sharp contrast to his performances throughout the season. Against the AFI qualifying standard of 13.63 seconds, the Tumakuru-native consistently delivered: 13.44 seconds (personal best) at the Indian Athletics Series (IAS) 6 in Chennai in early May; 13.52 seconds at the Senior Federation Cup in Ranchi later in May; and 13.55 seconds at the IAS 9 in Ludhiana in June.Reflecting on the setback, Krishik acknowledged his performance at the critical qualifying meet fell short. “I should have performed well at the Inter-State and secured at least a second position. Having said that, it’s only once in four years that we get an opportunity to represent India at the Asian Games,” he told TOI.When asked if his camp had appealed the decision, he added: “We did, but AFI insisted that I ought to have finished at least second at the Inter-State meet. I got three false starts in the final race. With even one foul, one comes under pressure, so I think that affected me.”Currently ranked seventh in Asia, the youngster remains focused on the immediate future. Looking ahead to the Indian Athletics Final Series in New Delhi today, Krishik remains defiant: “I'm 100% sure about winning and earning the qualification mark.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Correrá 900 kilómetros en 21 días... ¡para ver a Céline Dion en concierto!
articles.standfirst: La influencer Caroline Branaa iba a asistir al espectáculo de la cantante canadiense en 2020, pero se canceló, y ahora ideó este desafío para asegurarse tener las entradas
articles.summary: La influencer Caroline Branaa iba a asistir al espectáculo de la cantante canadiense en 2020, pero se canceló, y ahora ideó este desafío para asegurarse tener las entradas
articles.body: “Crecí con Céline Dion. Mis padres, mis tíos, mis tías, todos la escuchaban. Formó parte de mi infancia, de mi adolescencia, y aún lo es". La corredora e influencer Caroline Branaa es una admiradora de la cantante canadiense, a la que sigue desde su infancia. De hecho, tenía entradas para su concierto de 2020, que finalmente se canceló por la pandemia. Ahora, ante este nuevo espectáculo y antes incluso de que se pusieran a la venta las entradas, se fijó en otra influencer que ya tenía los tickets e ideó un reto: "Correré los 900 kilómetros hasta París si alguien me ofrece entradas", aseguró en su perfil de redes sociales. Poco después, la RTL (la emisora colaboradora del evento) se puso en contacto con ella en menos de 24 horas. Aunque ya tenía previstas otras carreras, como el maratón de París y el Hossegor Infinity Trail, empezó a preparar este desafío, pero el alto kilometraje hizo que tuviera que adaptar sus entrenamientos. "No sabía cómo prepararme para 900 kilómetros", admitía. "Al final lo he visualizado como una carrera de trail de 150 kilómetros y reorganizamos nuestro entrenamiento para que las carreras largas se acumularan, para que mi cuerpo entendiera que iba a afrontar largas distancias varios días seguidos. Mi carrera más larga fue de 80 km". La corredora saldrá de Hossegor este 12 de septiembre y dividirá el viaje en 21 días. El recorrido diario oscilará entre los 40 y 52 kilómetros, con un tramo final más corto para llegar algo más descansada. Pasará por Mimizan, Burdeos, Angoulême, Poitiers, Châtellerault y Orléans. Está previsto que llegue a la capital francesa el 2 de octubre... para asistir al concierto del día 3. "Mi la idea es descansar para poder disfrutar del concierto. No hay entradas para estar de pie, todos son asientos, lo cual es una suerte, porque Céline anunció un espectáculo de dos horas y estar de pie sería bastante duro"

articles.title: Connor McDavid has a special reason for loving Montreal, and Canadiens fans will absolutely appreciate his words
articles.summary: NHL News: Connor McDavid has never needed much convincing about what makes Montreal different. The Edmonton Oilers captain again made that clear while discussin.
articles.body: Connor McDavid has never needed much convincing about what makes Montreal different. The Edmonton Oilers captain again made that clear while discussing his experiences at Bell Centre, praising the building, the atmosphere and the Canadiens fan base. His comments are notable because Montreal has long been one of the NHL’s most intense stops for opposing stars. McDavid enjoys the cheers when he plays for Canada, but he also welcomes the boos when he arrives as an opponent. That contrast, he says, is part of what makes playing in Montreal so appealing.Why does Connor McDavid enjoy playing in Montreal?Connor McDavid’s attraction to Montreal comes down to the energy inside Bell Centre. He described the games there as intense and said those are exactly the kind of matchups he enjoys.“It always seems like an exciting game when we’re there. The energy of the building is there. It always feels intense. Those are the games I love to play honestly. It was special to play there for Canada (at the 4 Nations).”That last part matters. During the 4 Nations Face-Off, McDavid experienced Montreal from a different side. Instead of hearing the crowd turn against him because he wore an Oilers jersey, he received the kind of support usually reserved for the home team.He has also made it clear that he does not need the crowd to be friendly for the experience to be enjoyable. In fact, the hostility can add to it.“It’s nice to have the fans cheer for me there, but it’s also fun to play against (the Habs) and get the boos,” he said.For an opposing player, being booed is usually something to tolerate. McDavid sees it differently. The reaction tells him that the crowd is fully invested in the game.What did Connor McDavid say about Canadiens fans and Bell Centre?McDavid’s strongest praise was reserved for the relationship between Montreal and its team.“It’s such a special building to play in,” he said. “It’s such a great hockey town. The way (the fans) love their Canadiens is amazing.”There is an important distinction in those comments. McDavid was not simply praising the arena itself. He was talking about the culture surrounding the Canadiens. Montreal has a fan base that expects emotion, history and meaning from its hockey nights, and visiting stars feel that immediately.The comments have naturally caught attention because McDavid’s future in Edmonton remains a major NHL storyline. He signed a two-year extension last year, keeping him under contract through the 2027-28 season. That means Montreal is not suddenly a realistic destination because of a few compliments.Still, Canadiens fans can enjoy the moment. McDavid has praised Bell Centre before, including calling it one of his favorite buildings to play in. His latest comments simply reinforce something he has consistently said: Montreal brings out a different level of emotion, and he likes being part of it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Llegan los taxis autónomos a España y podrás cogerlos a finales de año
articles.standfirst: La alianza entre Uber y WeRide tiene ya la licencia de DGT para comenzar con la fase de pruebas. Madrid será la primera ciudad en disponer de este servicio
articles.summary: La alianza entre Uber y WeRide tiene ya la licencia de DGT para comenzar con la fase de pruebas. Madrid será la primera ciudad en disponer de este servicio
articles.body: Uber, en alianza con WeRide y Avomo, ha recibido la primera autorización nacional por parte de la Dirección General de Tráfico para operar con coches autónomos de nivel 4, lo que significa que son capaz de conducir de forma 100% autónoma y sin intervención humana. Así, y según ha informado Europa Press, tomar como servicio un taxi autónomo de Uber en la capital podría ser una realidad a finales de este mismo año. El permiso recibido permite a esta alianza iniciar la fase de despliegue de los vehículos autónomos, lo que requiere mapeo, validación de rutas y pruebas de preparación operativa. Para ello, se prevé contar con una veintena de vehículos dotados de la tecnología de conducción autónoma WeRide, que en esta fase de preparación llevarían a una persona a bordo supervisando todo el proceso. Este nuevo paso supone también dar luz verde a que pueda circular el monovolumen autónomo GXR de WeRide, que en breve debería aparecer por las zonas con gran demanda de taxis en la Comunidad de Madrid. La capital de España es la cuarta de las 15 ciudades en las que Uber y WeRide prevén desplegar sus vehículos autónomos antes de 2030. No se ha confirmado el número de vehículos que puede llegar a haber, pero en conjunto se asegura que serán decenas de miles los coches autónomos. Según Sarfraz Maredia, jefe global de Movilidad Autónoma y Reparto de Uber, "la Comunidad de Madrid se está consolidando rápidamente como uno de los entornos más avanzados de Europa para el desarrollo de esta tecnología, y estamos encantados de seguir trabajando junto a nuestros socios para contribuir a hacer realidad esa visión".

articles.title: Sergei Bobrovsky’s wife Olga bids emotional farewell to Florida as Toronto Maple Leafs chapter begins this NHL season
articles.summary: NHL News: Sergei Bobrovsky's wife Olga bids an emotional farewell to Florida as the veteran goaltender transitions to the Toronto Maple Leafs after a successful seven-year tenure with the Panthers.
articles.body: Toronto Maple Leafs goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky’s family is preparing for a big change after seven memorable years in South Florida. The veteran netminder embarks on a new chapter with Toronto, and his wife, Olga Bobrovsky, posted an emotional farewell to Florida.The move ends a major chapter in Bobrovsky’s career with the Florida Panthers, where he won two Stanley Cups and established himself as one of the NHL’s most decorated goaltenders.NHL star Sergei Bobrovsky’s wife Olga Bobrovsky says farewell to Florida Panthers eraOlga Bobrovsky said goodbye to the family's Florida chapter with an emotional social media post reflecting on the memories made during Sergei Bobrovsky's seven seasons with the Florida Panthers.The family's time in South Florida included two Stanley Cup championships, family milestones and countless moments away from the rink. Olga's departure was a reminder of how deeply the period had infiltrated the lives of the Bobrovskiys.In her message, Olga reflected on the family’s home in Florida and the memories that defined their time with the Panthers. She mentioned the seven-year contract, their two children and major personal moments during that time.The farewell comes as the Bobrovskys are about to move to Toronto after Sergei Bobrovsky leaves the Panthers. The move is a personal transition and a key career change for the veteran goaltender.Sergei Bobrovsky starts Toronto Maple Leafs chapterThis summer, Sergei Bobrovsky signed a three-year, $21 million deal with the Toronto Maple Leafs that set the stage for a stunning change for the 37-year-old goaltender.Toronto is getting a goaltender with plenty of NHL experience, two Vezina Trophy wins and a pair of Stanley Cup championships. Bobrovsky is expected to be a big part of the Maple Leafs’ quest for their first Stanley Cup since 1967.Bobrovsky also reunites with former goaltending partner Anthony Stolarz in the signing, adding yet another familiar face to Toronto’s crease.Florida Panthers captain Aleksander Barkov recently spoke highly of Bobrovsky and the impact he made on their time together.Barkov pointed to Bobrovsky’s work ethic and consistency, saying the veteran set an example for younger players. His comments highlight why Bobrovsky’s departure is more significant than his numbers.Over the last seven seasons, Bobrovsky has been a key reason why the Florida Panthers went from a non-contender to a Stanley Cup contender. His game helped lead the team to back-to-back titles in 2024 and 2025.What Sergei Bobrovsky brings to TorontoBobrovsky comes to Toronto with a long NHL resume and tonnes of postseason experience. His career record is 456-266-58, and he’s been able to stay healthy all 16 years in the NHL.His arrival brings Stanley Cup experience to a Toronto Maple Leafs team under pressure to end its long drought for the championship. The task ahead will be to transform Bobrovsky’s Florida success into another successful NHL chapter in Toronto.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Texas Longhorns LB Rasheem Biles earns SEC honors
articles.summary: Rasheem Biles is already making headlines. The talented linebacker was named the Southeastern Conference's Co-Defensive Player of the Week.
articles.body:
Just one game into his Longhorns career and Rasheem Biles is already making headlines. The talented linebacker was named the Southeastern Conference 's Co-Defensive Player of the Week on Monday, following a stellar performance against Texas State . In his first game in the burnt orange, Biles showed why he is a special player.

Against the Bobcats, Biles recorded five tackles with a half tackle for loss and forced two turnovers. His turnovers were a forced fumble and an interception that helped keep the momentum with the Longhorns . While the offense scored nearly 60 points, the defense showed it is a force to be reckoned with, with Biles leading the way.

As the Longhorns held Texas State to 349 yards of total offense, Biles was one of the team's best players. He finished third on the team in total tackles and was tied for first on the team in tackles for a loss. Regardless of the matchup, he made life difficult for the Texas State offense all afternoon.

On Saturday, he flashed the form that made him a star at Pittsburgh. He finished his Panthers career with 183 total tackles and 10.5 sacks. In his last season in the ACC, Biles set career highs in tackles with 100 and assists with 61. That is partly why he was a popular target in the portal.

For the Longhorns, Biles' successful debut was a welcome sign. He is expected to be a key piece of the defense and will be counted on against some of the country's best teams. If Biles can continue to build on his performance from the season opener, then more weekly awards will be on the horizon.

articles.title: Could Rally Chile offer Adrien Fourmaux the best chance at elusive WRC win?
articles.summary: Fourmaux now faces “a very good opportunity” to claim his first win in rallying’s top tier
articles.body:
After driving "as good as he's ever driven" in Paraguay, Rally Chile could present Adrien Fourmaux "a very good opportunity" to claim a maiden World Rally Championship victory, according to Hyundai Motorsport .

The Frenchman has been knocking on the door of an elusive first WRC win. The Hyundai factory driver came close in last year's Saudi Arabia season finale, however a check-in error while leading the event forced Fourmaux and co-driver Alex Coria to settle for second.

This year, Fourmaux has often led the Hyundai charge in terms of outright pace. A second place at Safari Rally Kenya came after losing more than two minutes on the opening stage.

Last time out in Paraguay, Fourmaux was again in the victory fight before punctures provided a setback. The 31-year-old, however, produced a head turning performance to fight back to third, after taking a minute out of the front runners, ending the rally with nine stages wins. Fourmaux declared after the rally that he felt he "deserved the victory".

Impressed by the drive in Paraguay, Hyundai sporting director Andrew Wheatley is convinced a first win will arrive sooner or later and believes this weekend's outing in Chile could provide an opportunity.

Adrien Fourmaux was in the fight for victory last time out

"It's [the first win] going to happen. There's no question," Wheatley told Motorsport.com. "He's now addressed and identified all of the challenges that were keeping him off the top step. I think his performance in Paraguay was about as good as he's ever driven.

"The reason why I say that is because his performance was consistent. Where he's making a positive impression at the moment is he drove every stage at a 100% and that's difficult to do, particularly in those challenging conditions.

"But that's how you win rallies by being consistent and consistently performing at a high level. And I think you know he's mentally pretty strong at the moment. I think it'll be a bit like Sami Pajari , who has won his first three WRC victories back-to-back [this year]. Once he can get that win off his shoulders, it will flow a lot easier.

"In terms of pure pace, we saw it earlier in the year in Safari where he dropped two minutes and 15 seconds on the first stage and finished second by 25 seconds. So that was annoying.

"Paraguay was equally annoying because he dropped around about three minutes with punctures and little problems over the weekend and again was able to take a minute out of Elfyn [Evans]. On Saturday, taking a minute out of a guy that's fighting for the world championship and a minute out of Sami as well is difficult.

"I believe the win is coming. I think this is probably a very good opportunity. He was fast here last year but if he can have the same rhythm that he had in Paraguay here, I think he could be ready to fight for a win."

Andrew Wheatley (left) believes a first win is coming for Fourmaux

Fourmaux showcased his speed in Chile last year after enjoying a spell in the lead before eventually finishing in third.

This weekend's event is expected to be largely dry, but the stages will be abrasive in places offering a high puncture risk. Crews will however have eight extra tyres at their disposal following a change in the regulations.

Road sweeping is also likely to be a factor, meaning road position will be crucial. Fourmaux will begin the rally from fifth on the road.

"I'm really looking forward to Rally Chile after showing very strong pace throughout the weekend in Paraguay – it gives us confidence and hopefully we can carry this performance into Chile," said Fourmaux.

"It's a rally I really enjoy, last year we were fighting at the front, and we finished on the podium. The stages are fast and flowing, but also quite technical, so you need a lot of precision and confidence in the car. We know we were competitive there last year, and after the performance we had in Paraguay, the target is to fight at the front again and push for the best possible result."

articles.title: Kentucky vs Alabama: Offensive X-Factors in week two
articles.summary: With Alabama coming to Lexington for a conference clash with Kentucky, we take a look at offensive X-factors in what could be a high scoring game.
articles.body:
Kentucky football hosts the Alabama Crimson Tide on Saturday for a massive SEC home opener. The Wildcats will be home underdogs and will try to shock the world by getting just their third ever win in the series. This might be a high scoring, shootout type of game, as both offenses are capable of big plays and scoring in bunches.

In this article, we will go through offensive X-factors for both teams and what to expect this weekend and what to expect on the offensive side of the ball. Let's take a look at some key players.

Kenny Minchey had a phenomenal debut in week one against Youngstown State in his first college start, now he gets his first SEC start against one of the best secondaries in the country. Minchey played a clean game in week one, and his operation of the offense did not look like a player making his first start. The offensive scheme will create misdirection and get playmakers open on this Alabama defense. I think a large part of this game comes down to which quarterback is more comfortable and consistent throughout the game.

Kentucky has a stable of tight ends that are difference makers, and they need to lean on them in this game. Willie Rodriguez had a team-high six targets in week one and will constantly be a threat to make plays in the passing game. Kentucky has two big outside receivers in Nic Anderson and DJ Miller, but they have a tough matchup against the corner duo of Zabien Brown and Dijon Lee. This tight end group can create mismatches in the passing game like we saw in week one, and I expect a ton of 12 and 13 personnel from Kentucky to get multiple tight ends on the field at the same time.

Rodriguez is the do-it-all tight end, but Skinner is a true X factor move tight end that has incredible athleticism. They will continue to find ways to get Skinner the football in space and he can showcase that athleticism. Skinner is tough to defend in open space and has a large catch radius. I expect the offense to lean on Rodriguez and Skinner in the passing game, and they will also help get the run game going in these two or three tight end sets.

Keelon Russell had a solid debut and will get the first SEC road start of his career on Saturday. He has to stay poised and make plays from the pocket, but as he showed in week one, he has the ability to extend plays with his legs which is something the Kentucky defense has to be aware of. Russell needs to play better than he did in week one for the Crimson Tide to get the win, and he has to lean on his dynamic playmakers. In a lot of ways, I truly think this game comes down to which quarterback can consistently play in rhythm and take care of the football.

Ryan Coleman-Williams had five catches for 130 yards in the season opener against ECU, but he still had a couple drops and had a few reps where the effort was lacking. Coleman-Williams has the potential to take the game over and will see a large target share on Saturday. Alabama needs the best of Coleman-Williams in Lexington this weekend, and there will be plenty of opportunities for him to make plays. The run game for the Crimson Tide remains a bit of a question mark, and if they can't get that going they will need to lean on the passing game.

articles.summary: Manchester United Tracking Nicolo Tresoldi as Tottenham Rivalry Builds After Club Brugge Scouting MissionManchester United’s recruitment team were back on th...
articles.body:
Manchester United Tracking Nicolo Tresoldi as Tottenham Rivalry Builds After Club Brugge Scouting Mission

Manchester United's recruitment team were back on the road this week, and the trip to Belgium may yet prove significant. According to TeamTalk , United and Tottenham both sent representatives to watch Club Brugge forward Nicolo Tresoldi on Tuesday evening, with the 22-year-old increasingly viewed as one of Europe's standout emerging attackers.

Tresoldi was on the scoresheet from the penalty spot in Brugge's 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa , and that appearance offered another timely reminder of why interest is building. TEAMtalk states that "Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur both had representatives in Belgium on Tuesday evening to watch Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi", underlining the level of attention now surrounding the German Under-21 international.

Nicolo Tresoldi emerging on Manchester United shortlist

This was not a one-player visit from United either. The report adds that the club "also used the trip to continue their work on left-back Joaquin Seys ", a player they had previously explored during the summer. That points to a broader Club Brugge assessment, though Tresoldi appears to be the name drawing the sharpest focus.

He arrives in this conversation with encouraging numbers and strong momentum. "He scored 23 goals last season", and those returns help explain why "his performances sparked considerable interest across the continent, with Barcelona among the clubs to hold talks over a potential move." Brugge managed to retain him, but the sense from this latest development is that his situation remains under close review.

Tottenham also pushing hard in Tresoldi race

Tottenham are firmly in the frame as well. TEAMtalk reports, "We can confirm Tottenham were also in Belgium to carry out further work on Tresoldi, who remains high on their radar." With Roberto De Zerbi looking to reinforce his attacking options, the striker is described as a player who "could develop into a strong option for the club."

That makes this one worth monitoring, particularly because both clubs have clear reasons to be active in the market. United "failed to add a forward over the summer and continue to assess attacking options for the future." There is also a notable line on Joshua Zirkzee , whose "future at Old Trafford remains in doubt after failing to force his way into Michael Carrick's starting XI."

Club Brugge talent offers flexibility for future planning

Perhaps the most revealing part of the report is the practical framing around United's next move. "United's position on the Dutchman remains the same – they won't let him go without first signing a replacement. Tresoldi could be that player." That is not the same as an imminent bid, but it does place the Brugge striker squarely in the thinking.

There is a wider picture too. Tresoldi "has rapidly established himself as one of the most exciting attacking prospects in Europe" and, if current form continues, "it seems only a matter of time before Tresoldi makes a high-profile switch to one of Europe's top sides." For now, the scouting stage continues, but both Manchester United and Tottenham appear to be gathering for a serious contest.

From a Manchester United perspective, this feels like the kind of move that makes a lot of sense if the club are planning carefully. Nicolo Tresoldi does not yet arrive with the noise of a finished superstar, but that can often be where the smartest recruitment lives. If United are genuinely looking for a forward with upside, athletic potential and room to grow, then this is exactly the profile they should be studying in detail.

The mention of Joshua Zirkzee is what really sharpens the debate. If the club "won't let him go without first signing a replacement", then United need to be absolutely certain on the next option. Tresoldi's numbers are promising, and the fact both United and Tottenham were there suggests he is being taken seriously at a high level. That alone raises the stakes.

There is also something encouraging about United doing multiple pieces of work in one trip, including Joaquin Seys. It hints at joined-up planning rather than opportunism. Supporters have wanted a more coherent recruitment model for years, and identifying players before the whole market explodes around them is part of that.

The obvious question is whether Tresoldi is ready for the pressure and physical demands of Old Trafford. That is where the scouting process matters. Watching him live, checking how he moves, how he reacts, how he influences a game beyond goals, all of that is crucial. On the face of it, this report is intriguing. United need more attacking certainty for the medium term, and Tresoldi sounds like a player worth serious attention.

articles.title: Celtics Star Jayson Tatum Reveals How 2025 Injury Change Him, Commemorates It Through His New Shoes
articles.summary: The 2025-27 season might be the worst in Jayson Tatum‘s career. He was not able to play much, and his team suffered one of the most painful playoff losses fo...
articles.body:
The 2025-27 season might be the worst in Jayson Tatum 's career. He was not able to play much, and his team suffered one of the most painful playoff losses for any player or team — blowing a 3-1 lead in a seven-game series.

Much of the blame is on the Boston Celtics forward's injury in the second round of the 2025 playoffs.

The Celtics faced off against the New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference semifinals, but their fate changed drastically when Tatum got injured in Game 4. It was a career performance for the six-time All-Star. He already had 42 points, eight rebounds, four assists, four steals, and two blocks under his name.

Unfortunately, he suffered an ACL injury in the final minute. It was eventually ruled a season-ending injury. The Celtics were eliminated in six games.

The 2017 No. 3 pick eventually returned in March, and the Celtics were among the best teams at that time, thanks in large part to Jaylen Brown , who was having an MVP-caliber season.

Tatum has been vocal about how traumatized he felt by that experience. He once discussed how he felt scared about returning to Madison Square Garden, where he suffered the injury.

"Nervousness, anxiousness, all the things you'd probably expect from the last time I played here. But it's a game," he said back in March.

Jayson Tatum still remembers the feeling

Six months into his successful return from the injury, Tatum admits that the event still haunts him. He confessed that he feels different because of the injury.

He will forever remember that painful moment, as he now commemorates it with his new shoe line. He released the Jordan Tatum 5, which he said was designed with his past injury in mind .

"On every Tatum 5, on the right side, there are five lines across the heel just to acknowledge the scar on my right heel," he during an event to launch the shoes (via Complex).

"What I've had to learn and also accept from that experience is, anytime you go through something traumatic, you're not the same you. You just can't be the same person anymore. And that's not saying that you're any worse, you're just different…So, aligning that with the Tatum 5, it looks different than every other shoe (I've had)."

Tatum will now head to the next season healthier and with bigger responsibilities as the team's lone star, following the shocking trade of Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers .

articles.title: Moreno Vs. Morales Odds, Full Fight Preview & Prediction
articles.summary: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Flyweight standouts Brandon Moreno vs. Joseph Morales will collide this weekend (Sat., Sept. 12, 2026) inside Desert Dia...
articles.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Flyweight standouts Brandon Moreno vs. Joseph Morales will collide this weekend (Sat., Sept. 12, 2026) inside Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Ariz., for Noche UFC 4 .

At 32 years of age, it feels like the best days of "The Assassin Baby" are behind him. That shouldn't be a shock given he's been fighting professionally for 15 years and 35 fights, but he's struck by an unusual case of inconsistency. Sometimes, Moreno still has the sharpened look of a champion, whereas other bouts see him falling over himself while loading up haymakers.

Either way, he's lost two straight leading to this co-main event versus red-hot Morales. "Bopo" was an unfortunate victim of the halfway Flyweight division dissolution of 2018 , and it took seven years for the prospect to return to the Octagon via The Ultimate Fighter (TUF) . Fortunately, two dominant victories via stoppage prove that Morales is back better than ever, and he's looking ready to make a run at gold.

Let's take a closer look at the betting odds and strategic keys for each athlete:

As mentioned in the intro, Moreno can be a frustrating fighter to watch. At his best, he can strike with anybody and possesses the division's best jab, as well as punishing kicks and counters. He doesn't have to just marching forward swinging loopy overhands, and yet that's what he does half of the time. Standup woes aside, Moreno is a slick grappler with strong wrestling.

What we have here is a good old-fashion collision of Mexican boxers that just so happens to take place inside a fenced cage. Sure, both Moreno and Morales are jiu-jitsu black belts, but they win a lot of exchanges and often bring fights to the floor via their boxing prowess. If you like matchups where mixed martial arts (MMA) fighters actually stand their ground and trade combos, this may end up as your " Fight of the Night. "

What's the most important weapon in a boxing match? The jab. What does Moreno neglect to utilize in most of his losses? The very same jab. Against Morales — a combination puncher with a powerful right hand — Moreno has to make use of his range advantage and continually pepper "Bopo" to interrupt his offense.

If Moreno's jab is flowing, everything tends to work well for the former champion.

Morales is a well-rounded athlete who specializes in boxing and jiu-jitsu. From top or bottom position, "Bopo" is really slick and able to wrap up submissions quickly. Despite having just two knockout wins on his record, Morales can crack as well, scoring plenty of his finishes via club-and-sub.

This is a matchup of boxers, and given the grappling/anti-wrestling prowess of both men, it feels likely to stay on the feet. In his UFC return versus Alibi Idiris , Morales found great success with consistent pressure, combinations, and body work. Against a brick-chinned vet like Moreno, he should also be trying to control the center and hit the midsection.

Moreno's recent losses have demonstrated a vulnerability to low kicks, and boxing exchanges should further expose his lead leg. I'd love to see Morales actively attacking the calf as a counter to jabs, as well as a punctuation mark to his combinations. If Morales can chew up Moreno's lead leg, everything else will grow easier.

Picking Moreno fights is no easy task. There's always a chance Moreno shows up looking like its 2022, and that version of "The Assassin Baby" would still be a title threat if he could show up consistently. Then, there's also a chance that Moreno shows up and falls over his own feet swinging his right hand — that guy is barely Top 15 .

Assuming we get something in the middle, it's hard not to favor the up-and-coming Morales. He has far fewer miles in the tank and has the power to hurt his opponent. If the two do end up on the mat, Morales' jiu-jitsu prowess should allow him to find his way to top position and spend more time overall in good position.

articles.title: No snap count restrictions for Chris Bell in Dolphins opener
articles.summary: Miami’s rookie receiver will be a full-go against Raiders in week one.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins may have struck gold when they nabbed wide receiver Chris Bell from Louisville in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. After all, the player was projected to be a late first round pick prior to his ACL tear in November of last year. Due to that injury, many thought that Bell would be eased back into action — possibly missing the first half of his rookie season. However, Bell's recovery has been an expeditious one, and the receiver has been named a starter for the Dolphins ahead of their Week One clash in Las Vegas against the Raiders .

And according to new head coach Jeff Hafley, Bell will be a full-go and will not be on a snap count when he takes the field on Sunday.

Yesterday, while speaking with the South Florida media, Hafley confirmed that Bell will have no restrictions against Las Vegas.

"We're going to play him — see how he feels — but, there's no pitch count on Chris."

Bell's full availability is an extremely positive development for the Dolphins, especially this early in the season. Quarterback Malik Willis will have a full complement of weapons for his first start with Miami — including fellow rookies Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr., as well as Malik Washington and tight end Greg Dulcich . Of course, Miami's most explosive offensive player, De'Von Achane, will factor mightily into this tilt as well.

Will that be enough to allow Miami to sneak past Las Vegas? We will all find out in just a few short days.

articles.title: Pakistan U19 cricketers mistaken for asylum seekers by protesters in UK
articles.summary: The English cricket board confirms it is reviewing the team’s security for the remainder of the tour.
articles.body:
Pakistan’s Under-19 cricket team has found itself at the centre of an anti-migrant protest in the United Kingdom after a group of masked protesters mistook the players for asylum seekers and gathered outside the team’s hotel.

Protesters in Portsmouth gathered outside the Marriott on Tuesday night, believing busloads of asylum seekers were being brought to the four-star hotel, only to be told that it was Pakistan’s U-19 cricket team on tour.

British media first reported the incident, and the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) confirmed that it was reviewing the team’s security for the remainder of the tour and had reached out to the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB).

Al Jazeera reached out to the PCB but did not receive a comment.

Sumair Syed, PCB’s chief operating officer, told the BBC that the team reported people “knocking on their doors” during the incident, but the players “behaved responsibly and didn’t escalate the situation”.

The team continued with their scheduled match the following day, which they won by 177 runs.

Syed described the incident as “unfortunate” but said he was in contact with the ECB, which had “assured us that every possible measure should be taken for the security of the escort”.

“This is the responsibility of the whole sport to ensure the safety, security and wellbeing of the visiting team,” he said. “They are on it, and we are hopeful that nothing of such sort will happen in the future.”

Tuesday’s incident at the hotel comes in the wake of anti-migrant protests in Portsmouth earlier in the week.

British media reported that hundreds of protesters clashed with the police in Portsmouth on Sunday evening after a dinghy carrying asylum seekers was brought into the UK.

Reform county councillor George Madgwick, who was called to mediate the incident on Tuesday night, has repeatedly defended those protesting against the arrival of migrants in the UK.

“The left are losing their minds that a handful of people went to a hotel, by accident, when they thought migrants had been bussed in. Once they discovered it was incorrect they left swiftly. Literally nothing happened,” he wrote in a post on X on Wednesday night.

“If Labour fixed the small boat crisis this issue would stop,” Madgwick went on to say.

Madgwick did not respond when contacted by Al Jazeera.

articles.title: Why is Alex Formenton’s Edmonton Oilers signing creating controversy across the NHL before the season
articles.summary: NHL News: The Edmonton Oilers' recent signing of Alex Formenton brings considerable controversy tied to the 2018 Hockey Canada case. As Formenton aims for a roster spot, the implications of this legal history could impact the NHL dynamics this season.
articles.body: Edmonton Oilers sign Alex Formenton to a one-year, $850,000 contract, marking the forward's return to the NHL after a three-year stint with HC Ambri-Piotta in Switzerland. The deal provides the 26-year-old a chance to compete for a roster spot heading into the 2026-27 season.However, Formenton’s involvement in the legal proceedings surrounding the 2018 Hockey Canada case has made the signing one of the most closely followed NHL roster moves of the offseason. Formenton was acquitted of the criminal charge, and other developments related to Hockey Canada’s disciplinary process continue to shape the discussion around his return.Why did Edmonton Oilers sign Alex Formenton now? The Edmonton Oilers have agreed to terms with Alex Formenton to add an experienced forward at a relatively low salary as they prepare for the upcoming NHL season, and the one-year contract has an average annual value of $850,000 and runs through the 2026-27 season.Formenton has NHL experience, speed and penalty-killing ability coming to the Edmonton Oilers. He appeared in 109 regular-season games with the Ottawa Senators, registering 23 goals and 16 assists. His best NHL season came in 2021-22 when he scored 18 goals and had 32 points in 79 games.His productivity, too, has remained steady during his time overseas. Formenton played three seasons in Switzerland with HC Ambri-Piotta, scoring 33 goals and 52 points in 88 games. That experience could aid him in fighting for a bottom-six spot when Edmonton’s training camp kicks off.What does Alex Formenton bring to Edmonton Oilers?Much of the controversy surrounding the signing has to do with the 2018 Hockey Canada case involving Formenton and four of his former teammates. The NHL had reinstated all five players before the criminal trial, which ended in Formenton’s acquittal, making them eligible to return to league play.But the larger disciplinary context is still in the conversation. The independent appeal board said the players breached Hockey Canada’s code of conduct, with different timelines for eligibility for the players involved. The latest developments mean that only Formenton is eligible to be reinstated to Hockey Canada-sanctioned programs.How could the signing affect Edmonton Oilers?If Formenton finds himself a regular spot on the roster, the immediate hockey impact could be huge. Edmonton has questions about its forward depth to start the season due to injuries, including problems with Matt Savoie and Mattias Janmark, so Formenton comes with an opportunity to fight for real minutes rather than just being a long-term organisational addition.The $850,000 deal also reduces the financial risk of the move from a salary-cap perspective. Formenton has not played an NHL game since the 2021-22 season, and training camp and preseason performances will be the clearest indication of whether his speed and scoring ability can translate back to NHL competition.So the Edmonton Oilers’ decision is about more than just adding another forward, and it’s a cheap gamble on a roster that has a player whose return is of considerable public interest. Formenton will be hoping to build on that chance with a lasting return to the ice in the coming NHL season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Alice Kinsella: British gymnast continues historic comeback at international level
articles.summary: A year after giving birth, Alice Kinsella takes the latest step on her groundbreaking return to gymnastics at an international meeting for Great Britain.
articles.body:
Olympic gymnast Alice Kinsella says it is "hard to put into words" how she feels about returning to international competition as her groundbreaking comeback to the sport continues this weekend.

The two-time European champion became the first British artistic gymnast to resume elite competition after giving birth, when she finished fourth in the beam at the British Championships in March.

Now the 25-year-old is preparing for her first competition back in Great Britain colours at a senior team international against France, Switzerland, Germany and Italy at Fenton Manor in Stoke on 12-13 September.

"It's kind of crazy - it's such a surreal feeling but I am very excited," Kinsella told BBC Radio Stoke.

"It's only been a year, postpartum. Training-wise, it's been tough, but it's been good. I'm excited to finally get out there. I'm ready, I'm doing everything I can to get back where I was.

"It's been a rollercoaster but a good one."

Kinsella's pioneering journey back to the sport is so rare it became the subject of a university research paper into elite gymnasts resuming their careers after giving birth.

Her son Parker, who was born in September 2025, is already a source of inspiration and he will be watching his mum compete at the weekend as Kinsella competes in all four pieces of apparatus - balance beam, bars, vault and floor - for the first time.

"It's really special because I've wanted to try to get back into a team and this is a really good start because it's a little four-way," said Kinsella, who trains with Park Wrekin Gymnastics Club in Shropshire.

"It's not too big of a competition, which is really good. I'm definitely nervous, but it's hard to put into words - it's been so long.

"I did the British [Championships] in March but only did beam and that's all I was training really, but now I'm trying to do all four so it's more on the body.

"It's not like you've done one piece and you can stop thinking about everything, you've got to move on to the next and think about that. So it's been tough."

Pioneering gymnast targets rare return to elite competition after baby

'For my boy' - Kinsella makes GB gymnastics history

Gymnastics now more a mental challenge - Kinsella

Putting GB leotard back on 'feels very weird'

After revealing she only took "three or four weeks off" after giving birth, Kinsella returned to training at the start of the year with the longer-term intention of being at the World Championships in China in 2027 and the Olympics in Los Angeles in 2028.

But, after finding herself ahead of schedule so far this year, she wanted to take the chance to step it up.

"My main goal was to try to get back next year but I'm actually a lot further forward than I thought I would be," added Kinsella, who won bronze in the team event at the Tokyo Olympics in 2020.

"So that's why I'm doing this competition because I just want to get out there, compete, because I don't like doing nothing."

What makes Kinsella's return so unique are the obvious challenges - and changes to the body - pregnancy and childbirth brings.

There are many examples of women returning to the top of their sports after becoming mothers but gymnastics, where vital pelvic floor and core strength are both weakened during pregnancy, is different.

Kinsella said her gymnastics background has played a big part in her being able to return to physical exercise so quickly but said she "didn't feel too bad" when she got back in the gym.

"I always had that goal to get back into the gym and I think when I've got a goal set I will do everything I can to achieve it," she said.

"Getting back into a leotard with how my body's changed just feels very weird, but I guess that shows what my body has gone through and I try to think about it in a positive way."

Her body is not the only thing that has changed with Kinsella adding that parenthood has helped her become better at taking the pressure off herself as an athlete.

"Having a baby changes your life - I'm very patient, whereas before Parker I was not patient at all," she said.

"When I made one tiny mistake I would get so annoyed, but now if I just make like a little mistake I'm totally fine about it.

"You have to be patient with kids, they're crazy. So I've definitely changed in that aspect but style-wise and gymnastics-wise like I don't think that's changed.

"Things are harder to get back and to do but I think the more I train it'll probably feel a lot easier."

Kinsella said when she started her comeback "no one really had any idea what I was going to able to do" and wants to keep levels of expectation for her international return as realistic as possible.

For her, this weekend in Stoke is there primarily "just to enjoy it" and to "get the experience of all four pieces [of apparatus] again".

"My body's changed, I can't do the same amount of training I used to do but I'm definitely getting back to that," Kinsella said.

"We're definitely on the right track to be where I was before I had Parker. My goal was to start competing next year properly on all four.

"It's going to be really fun. Whatever happens, happens, good, bad. I'm just proud I'm able to be back out there a year postpartum."
