articles.title: Days before Asian Games, Tanya Chaudhary shatters national record in big boost for Indian athletics
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Indian athletics received a major boost just days before the Asian Games as Uttar Pradesh's Tanya Chaudhary shattered the women's hammer th.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian athletics received a major boost just days before the Asian Games as Uttar Pradesh's Tanya Chaudhary shattered the women's hammer throw national record at the Indian Athletics Series Final on Thursday.Tanya sent the hammer to a distance of 68.35m, bettering the previous national record of 67.02m set by her state-mate Anushka Yadav in June. Anushka finished second with a best effort of 66.34m.Both Tanya and Anushka are part of India's Asian Games squad, making Tanya's record-breaking performance particularly significant with the Games beginning on September 19.Tanya pocketed Rs 1 lakh for winning the event, while Anushka received Rs 50,000.A huge jump from Tanya's last Asian Games outingThe new national record represents a massive improvement from Tanya's previous Asian Games performance. She finished seventh at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou with a throw of 60.50m.Her latest effort of 68.35m is also well beyond the 64.14m that earned South Korea's Kim Tae-hui the women's hammer throw bronze medal in Hangzhou.With the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games now just days away, Tanya's breakthrough provides an encouraging sign for India's athletics contingent and could give her significant momentum heading into the competition.Expanded athletics squad adds to India's strengthThe Athletics Federation of India had initially named a 77-member athletics squad — 34 men and 43 women — for the 20th Asian Games in Japan. The contingent has since been expanded to 79 athletes.The squad features several Asian and national record holders, including Gulveer Singh, Avinash Sable, Sreeshankar M, Ancy Sojan, Praveen Chithravel, Tejaswin Shankar, Rohit Yadav, Annu Rani, Jyothi Yarraji and Priyanka Goswami.India's overall Asian Games contingent has also been expanded to 503 athletes across 36 sports, following the inclusion of surfing.Athletics, which will be without injured javelin star Neeraj Chopra, has the largest support staff among India's disciplines, with 31 members, including 20 coaches led by national coach P Radhakrishnan.Tanya's national record has thus arrived at an ideal time, giving Indian athletics another timely boost ahead of the Games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: En el Día Mundial de la Prevención del Suicidio, la alpinista recuerda los problemas de salud mental que atravesó y asegura que "no estás solo, se puede encontrar un camino, pide ayuda"
articles.body: Edurne Pasaban, la primera mujer en coronar las 14 cimas más altas del planeta, ha hecho hincapié en numerosas ocasiones de la importancia de la salud mental, sobre todo tras recuperarse de la depresión que sufrió en el momento más álgido de su carrera deportiva. Así, en el Día Mundial para la Prevención del Suicidio, la alpinista aseguró que "siempre hablo de la importancia de la salud mental y no me cansaré de hacer lo que esté en mis manos para que podamos seguir construyendo un futuro donde la salud mental no sea solo un tema sobre la mesa o un debate, sino una realidad que conlleve herramientas, inversión, personas, conocimiento. Paso a la acción". Pasaban recordó en sus redes sociales que "en España alrededor de 11 personas mueren cada día por suicidio y yo un día casi fui una de esas once (...). Hoy estoy aquí para decirte algo que en aquel momento yo no podía ver: se puede salir" La alpinista recordó que "cuando estás sufriendo muchísimo parece que no hay otra opción (...). Pero eso que sientes hoy no tiene que ser para siempre, se puede encontrar un camino. No es fácil, lo sabemos, pero se puede". Edurne también destacó la importancia que tienen el entorno de la persona que atraviesa problemas de salud mental. "No penséis que tenéis que encontrar las palabras perfectas para estar a nuestro lado. A veces simplemente quedarse al lado y acompañar es muchísimo". Por último, la alpinista recordó que "si estás pasando por esto, por favor, pide ayuda. Porque pedir ayuda no es rendirse. Pedir ayuda es elegir quedarse"

articles.title: Phil Kessel, Amanda Kessel Headline U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame's Class of 2026
articles.summary: Siblings Phil and Amanda Kessel were named to the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame's class of 2026 on Thursday.
articles.body:
Siblings Phil and Amanda Kessel were named to the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame's class of 2026 on Thursday.

USA Hockey announced that T.J. Oshie, Ryan Suter and Stan Wong will be inducted alongside the Kessels as well:

Trades That Could Happen Before Training Camp

Per NHL.com's Tom Gulitti , the five inductees will be enshrined in the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame on Nov. 30 in Washington, D.C.

Phil and Amanda Kessel are only the second brother-sister pairing to be inducted into the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame, joining Tony and Cammi Granato, who were enshrined in 2020 and 2008, respectively.

The 38-year-old Phil Kessel played 17 NHL seasons with the Boston Bruins, Toronto Maple Leafs, Pittsburgh Penguins, Arizona Coyotes and Vegas Golden Knights.

A three-time All-Star and three-time Stanley Cup champion, Kessel recorded 414 goals and 992 points in 1,286 career NHL regular-season games, and he holds the NHL record for most consecutive games played with 1,064.

Kessel twice represented Team USA in the Winter Olympics, winning a silver medal in 2010. He also won a gold medal and a silver medal for the U.S. in the IIHF U18 World Championship.

Amanda Kessel, 35, played forward for Team USA at three Olympics, winning gold in 2018, and silver in both 2014 and 2022.

She also won IIHF Women's World Championship gold medals in 2013, 2017, 2019 and 2023, and silver medals in 2012, 2021 and 2022.

Kessel retired from playing in 2024, and she is the current assistant general manager for the AHL's Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins.

Oshie played 16 NHL seasons with the St. Louis Blues and Washington Capitals from 2008 to 2024, registering 302 goals and 695 assists in 1,010 games.

The skilled forward was a one-time All-Star and one-time Stanley Cup champion, and he played for Team USA at one Olympics, three World Championships, one World Junior Championship and one World Cup of Hockey.

Suter will join his uncle, longtime NHL defenseman Gary Suter, as a member of the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame.

Ryan Suter played 20 NHL seasons with the Nashville Predators, Minnesota Wild, Dallas Stars and Blues, earning three career All-Star selections.

Suter had 107 goals and 589 assists for 696 points, and his 1,526 career games played are the second-most ever by a U.S.-born defenseman behind only Chris Chelios.

Suter played for Team USA at two Olympics, winning a silver medal at the 2014 Sochi Games. He also won gold in the World Junior Championship, the World U-17 Hockey Challenge and the IIHF U18 World Championship.

Wong, 68, is a longtime athletic trainer for USA Hockey, serving in that role at five Olympics, 19 World Championships and 24 World Junior Championships, per Gulitti.

articles.title: Rams' travel gamble could give 49ers the edge in Thursday Night Football's Australia opener
articles.summary: The 49ers flew to Melbourne a week early while the Rams landed Tuesday, creating a massive travel edge for Thursday Night Football in Australia.
articles.body: Goo’day mate, shall we throw a bet on the barby? If you don’t understand the reason for that opener, then you might want to double-check your location for this game. The NFL is heading to Australia for the game today between the 49ers and Rams, which means we have our first Thursday Night Football action of the new season. The San Francisco 49ers had a rather disappointing end to their 2025 season. They went into the playoffs looking like one of the more complete teams in football, and they were rinsed by the Seahawks basically from opening kickoff. This year they come in healthy, but there are an awful lot of questionable designations next to their lineup. They have six players on offense, including Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle, listed as questionable. Their defense isn’t looking much better, with five guys listed, including Nick Bosa. Fred Warner is healthy, though, so that’s a good sign. If the team is fully healthy, it should be among the better in football. Even when the 49ers haven’t been healthy, they’ve had a strong next-man-up attitude that has made them stay in contention. INJURY BUG BITES 49ERS AGAIN AS TEAM LOSES KEY DEFENSIVE TACKLE DURING PRACTICE IN AUSTRALIA The Los Angeles Rams are a super team. It is almost comical looking at their roster. If the Pro Bowl was a thing, you’d basically call this roster a Pro Bowl roster. They were the only team to put up a true fight against Seattle in the playoffs, and they lost a back-and-forth battle. In the offseason, they added Myles Garrett via trade, and then that drew Aaron Donald out of retirement. A bit of good fortune for the 49ers is that Donald will not suit up. Offensively, the Rams are still one of the most elite teams in football. It hinges on the health of Matthew Stafford, but he is coming off of an MVP season and arguably the best one of his career. He still has Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to throw the ball to. The team is extremely deep, and the Rams have a creative coach that won’t let them rest on offense. AARON DONALD WILL NOT TRAVEL TO AUSTRALIA FOR RAMS OPENER AGAINST 49ERS AS TEAM RAMP-UP PROCESS NOT COMPLETE This game being in Melbourne does throw a wrench into the betting strategy. If it was in Los Angeles, the Rams would probably be -4.5 favorites, and you probably just take them and move on. Instead, the game is overseas. Travel plays a major factor in this game. The 49ers flew to Australia a week ago and will be completely adjusted to the time difference. SEAN MCVAY EXPECTS EVERY RAMS PLAYER TO BE ON FLIGHT TO AUSTRALIA FOR WEEK 1, INCLUDING AARON DONALD The Rams, however, flew on Tuesday. That means they essentially land, then sleep, wake up, and play football. It is a 14-16 hour flight. They are also leaving two hours after the game is over. It is an interesting strategy, but the team apparently doesn’t want them to adjust. Traveling internationally is difficult. I expect the Rams to start rather slowly. The 49ers should have the upper hand at least through the first half of the game, as the Rams' bodies will still be off. Give me the 49ers with the points in this game. I just don’t think the Rams will ever get the separation needed, but they should win the game. articles.title: Mona Agarwal secures LA 2028 Paralympic quota with silver at World Championships
articles.summary: More sports News: NEW DELHI: Indian para-shooter Mona Agarwal secured a quota place for the 2028 Paralympic Games in Los Angeles after winning silver in the women’s 10m.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian para-shooter Mona Agarwal secured a quota place for the 2028 Paralympic Games in Los Angeles after winning silver in the women’s 10m Air Rifle Standing SH1 event at the WSPS World Championships in Changwon, South Korea, on Thursday.The 38-year-old finished with a score of 250.0, just 0.2 points behind Serbia’s 22-year-old Kristina Trifunovic, who claimed gold with 250.2. The top two finishers were eligible for the coveted Paralympic quota places, meaning Agarwal’s silver earned India its first quota in the event.For Agarwal, the achievement also marked her maiden World Championships medal. She had previously won silver in the same event at the Changwon World Cup last year.From missing quota by 0.3 to securing LA placeThe quota was particularly meaningful for Agarwal because of her experience at the 2023 World Championships, when she narrowly missed out on qualification.“Last time in 2023 when I had participated in the World Championships, I missed the quota by 0.3. It was my second international match and I was very nervous,” Agarwal told RevSportz.“I still have those memories fresh in my mind. I participated this time with all those learnings and I am happy that I could achieve whatever I wanted to. So, the performance this time and the medal means a lot to me,” she added.Agarwal, who hails from Sikar in Rajasthan and was afflicted with polio as an infant, won a bronze medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games.She recalled another memorable moment from her journey.“I remember in March 2024 during the New Delhi World Cup, I was told that you have the last ‘bacha-hua’ quota. I considered even that as a glory but this time I am grateful to almighty that he supported me and I could secure the first quota place,” she said.Avani wins bronze as India clinch team goldParis Paralympics gold-medallist Avani Lekhara also finished on the podium, taking bronze with 229.4. However, she could not secure a quota as only the top two finishers were eligible.Agarwal and Lekhara combined to help India win the team gold medal in the event.Agarwal already has her sights set on Los Angeles.“In 2028, I want the medal colour to change into a Gold and I am also planning to secure a medal in the 50m event, since it would be my first achievement in 50m if I get one,” she said.“In shooting and para-shooting, the quota place belongs to the country and not the individual athlete who secures it. articles.body: El futuro del capitán de la Selección Colombia, James Rodríguez, sigue siendo uno de los principales focos de atención en el mercado de pases. Tras quedar en condición de agente libre luego del cierre del libro de pases en Europa, el mediocampista cucuteño recibió una propuesta formal del US Avellino, conjunto que compite en la Serie B de Italia. De acuerdo con los últimos reportes emitidos desde Italia y confirmados por medios locales, James y su entorno habrían desestimado el primer ofrecimiento contractual del club de la Campania. La oferta inicial rondaba entre 1 y 2.5 millones de euros por temporada más bonos, cifras que fueron catalogadas como bajas para las aspiraciones del '10'. A pesar de la negativa inicial, las conversaciones no están cerradas. La directiva del Avellino, encabezada por su proyecto deportivo para lograr el ascenso a la Serie A, ha presentado un nuevo ofrecimiento económico ajustado con el objetivo de convencer al futbolista colombiano. La posibilidad de ver a James vestir la camiseta del Avellino ha causado un enorme impacto interno en la escuadra italiana: A sus 35 años, las intenciones de James Rodríguez se centran en mantener continuidad competitiva que le permita seguir en la órbita de Néstor Lorenzo y la Selección Colombia de cara a los próximos retos internacionales. Al encontrarse en calidad de jugador libre, James no está sujeto a la ventana de transferencias convencional y puede ser inscrito por cualquier club que disponga de cupos en su plantilla. Se espera que en las próximas horas se defina si el Avellino realiza un esfuerzo financiero definitivo o si el entorno del colombiano evalúa otras alternativas en el fútbol internacional.

articles.standfirst: Escándalo en el FPC: Denuncian grave corrupción y pagos irregulares en el fútbol colombiano
articles.summary: Escándalo en el FPC: Denuncian grave corrupción y pagos irregulares en el fútbol colombiano
articles.body: El Fútbol Profesional Colombiano vuelve a ser centro de controversia. Tras los recientes escándalos sobre presuntas apuestas deportivas que involucran a jugadores de los torneos de la Dimayor, una nueva y contundente revelación ha sacudido las estructuras del balompié nacional: la exigencia o aceptación de cobros económicos para alinear futbolistas. La denuncia fue hecha por Stalin Motta, emblemático exmediocampista y capitán histórico de La Equidad, quien también vistió las camisetas de Atlético Nacional y Cúcuta Deportivo. En declaraciones entregadas a Gol Caracol y recogidas por la revista Semana, Motta expuso los oscuros manejos que presenció antes de su retiro del fútbol profesional: "Yo cuando salí del fútbol, salí muy triste, decepcionado de muchas cosas que no tienen que estar presentes, como el de los malos manejos de los directivos, como que jueguen jugadores profesionalmente no por su capacidad, sino por otros temas, como temas económicos (jugadores) que ponen dinero", expresó el ex jugador. El exjugador bogotano precisó que estas prácticas se mantenían vigentes hasta el momento de su salida de las canchas: "Cuando me retiré, hace ya 3 años, sí pagaban, no sé a quién, pero sí lo hacían". Motta relató que la diferencia entre el rendimiento deportivo de las prácticas y las decisiones finales en las convocatorias generaba constante asombro e indignación dentro del camerino. "No sé, me quieres ver en una cárcel, yo quiero estar con mi familia... Algunos estaban por encima de jugadores que trabajan día tras día", aclara. Futbolistas con menor nivel o trabajo diario terminaban jugando por encima de aquellos que se esforzaban semana a semana. "Uno se daba cuenta en las concentraciones cuando salían unos y entraban otros. Uno decía; ¿qué pasa aquí?...Guau", señala.

articles.title: Gimme him: One player the Bears would steal from the Panthers
articles.summary: Here is one player that the Chicago Bears would steal from the Carolina Panthers that would boost their secondary.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears are set to take on the Carolina Panthers in their season opener this Sunday, and as both teams appeared to have their offenses set, they're both coming into this year with question marks on defense.

Despite a sub .500 record last season, the Panthers made it to the playoffs but were eliminated in the wild-card round. This season they are set to be in contention and what should be a wide-open NFC South division, partially because of some under the radar members of their defense.

Each week here at Bears Wire we are picking one player from the opposing team who we would steal and put on the Bears. This week it's Panthers cornerback Jaycee Horn .

Defense will be key for the Bears this season and, after losing cornerback Nahshon Wright and safeties Jaquan Brisker and Kevin Byard in free agency and with Chicago expected to be without safety Coby Bryant for most of the season and cornerback Kyler Gordon on injured reserve, the team's secondary is in full focus.

Jaycee Horn has been one of the most underrated cornerbacks in the league, and he has not settled on any of his success early in his career. The former eighth overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft is a two-time Pro Bowl selection, who made it clear that the next step he wants is to have an All-Pro honor added to his resume.

The Bears have Jaylon Johnson as their top cornerback, but putting Horn on the opposite side of Johnson would give defensive coordinator Dennis Allen two corners who can shut down the opposition. An added benefit to putting Horn on the Bears is the thought of what defensive backs coach Al Harris could do with two elite talent corners leading the way in his secondary, and how it would open up more opportunities for the rest of the defensive backs on Chicago's defense.

Augustine, a South Lyon native and former Michigan State star, was one of the premier goaltenders in the NCAA the last two years. articles.title: Celtic 5-1 Rangers – Men against boys as Celtic do their talking on the field
articles.summary: On this day in 2016 – Men against boys as Celtic do their talking on the field. Here’s an extract from INVINCIBLE by Matt Corr….Moussa Dembelle of Celtic cel...
articles.body:
On this day in 2016 – Men against boys as Celtic do their talking on the field. Here's an extract from INVINCIBLE by Matt Corr….

Moussa Dembelle of Celtic celebrates after scoring his third goal during the Scottish Premier league match between Celtic and Rangers at Celtic Park Stadium on September 10, 2016. (Photo by Jeff J Mitchell/Getty Images)

New signing Cristian Gamboa was deemed ready for a place on the bench as Mark Warburton brought his Rangers team across Glasgow on Saturday, 10 September 2016 for the first meeting of the sides since the ill-fated shoot-out at Hampden, five months earlier.

Brendan Rodgers made just the one, enforced change, Moussa Dembele replacing the injured Leigh Griffiths . It would prove to be a very significant hand dealt by fate indeed. Some things are just meant to be, I guess.

The teams appeared in the tunnel to a deafening roar from 58,348 fans, Celts emerging to face a human tricolour in the north-east corner where the Ultras assemble, one of the most visually effective displays I have ever seen in five decades supporting the famous Hoops.

Celtic fans hold up a banner during the Scottish Premier league match between Celtic and Rangers at Celtic Park on September 10, 2016. (Photo by Jeff J Mitchell/Getty Images)

Once again, Celtic started in dominant mood, forcing the play, however, we had passed the half-hour mark before the first goal arrived, Scott Sinclair 's curling corner met by a majestic header from Dembele, which bulleted past Wes Foderingham in the Rangers goal.

As the noise levels increased yet further, Dembele made it a derby double, running onto Nir Bitton 's through ball to check back inside Philippe Senderos , the former Arsenal defender left unceremoniously grounded as the Frenchman struck an exquisite right-footed finish around Foderingham and into the far corner for 2-0.

Brendan Rodgers manager of Celtic at the end with Mark Warburton manager of Rangers after the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Rangers on September 10, 2016. (Photo by Steve Welsh/Getty Images)

Seconds before half-time, the visitors pulled a goal back, literally out of the blue, Kenny Miller 's header across the six-yard box bundled in by Joe Garner , to slightly dampen the party atmosphere over the interval.

The Hoops fans needn't have worried. On 60 minutes, Mikael Lustig prompted Dembele into life with a pass delivered in from the right flank. This time Moussa deceived the back-peddling Rangers defence by threading a delightful pass through to Sinclair, his clinical one-touch finish clipping the post on its way to making it 3-1, Scott's fourth successive League goal.

Moussa Dembele of Celtic scores his 2nd goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Rangers on September 10, 2016. (Photo by Steve Welsh/Getty Images)

The unfortunate Senderos' afternoon then went from bad to worse, with 15 minutes remaining, the big Swiss defender stretching up to stop another attack with his hands, leaving referee Collum no option but to show him a second yellow card.

There would be more pain to endure for Warburton's promoted side. As the clock ticked on to 83 minutes, Lustig sent over a perfect cross, which took stand-in central defender Joey Barton out of the game completely. Dembele's finish was sublime, one touch to control before firmly placing the ball into the far corner with his left foot for the perfect hat-trick, his first treble in senior football.

The icing on the Celtic cake was provided right at the death, this time Kieran Tierney the provider, his cross from the left picking out Stuart Armstrong . The blond midfielder, a replacement for Rogic early in the second half, momentarily appeared to have missed his opportunity, drifting past defenders only to strike it back across the keeper and in for 5-1.

It was party central in the east end of Glasgow.

This would be the first significant checkpoint in the 2016/17 title race. Celtic, having won at Tynecastle and Perth and then scored nine goals at home to the two anticipated main challengers, Aberdeen and Rangers, had a 100% record, already four points clear of the Ibrox side with a game n hand.

It had been a perfect start to the domestic season, with recent signings Moussa Dembele and Scott Sinclair contributing more than their fair share of goals, whilst Leigh Griffiths had continued where he had left off in May. And all achieved against a background of Champions League qualification and injuries to key players.

It was, therefore, a happy Brendan Rodgers who spoke to the press after the game, asked first, of course, about the performance of his exciting young French striker.

Moussa Dembele of Celtic scores his 3rd goal ( Celtics 4th)with during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Rangers on September 10, 2016. (Photo by Steve Welsh/Getty Images)

"He was outstanding. He was up against Philippe Senderos, who's an experienced player – but you see his physicality in the game, his heading ability, his running ability and a wonderful touch and finish."

And his views on the game and the experience overall?

"I was disappointed that we conceded a goal before half-time. You expect them to come out and try to force the game in the first 10 minutes of the second half and there was too much area opening up, especially in the central areas – so we made the change.

"Tom's had a lot of travel in the international break. We said to Stu that this was a game he could come into and look to press and work and he's done that very well and got his goal. He contributed to a great team performance."

Scott Sinclair of Celtic scores during the Scottish Premier league match between Celtic and Rangers at Celtic Park at Celtic Park Stadium on September 10, 2016. (Photo by Jeff J Mitchell/Getty Images)

"It was important to win today and keep the momentum going. We have got to be relentless in our quest to win the title again and that was a good marker for us. The atmosphere today was truly special. When the noise is like that, it really is a team that has a 12th man.

"They had a real disappointment at Hampden only a few months back, so hopefully they have shown the improvements they have made. It is great for the supporters. It is always about bragging rights for the supporters, and I think they will be proud of their team today."

Man-of-the-moment Dembele could scarcely contain his delight, admitting that it was an experience he would remember "for my whole life."

Moussa Dembele of Celtic celebrates his 2nd goal with Scott Sinclair during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Rangers at Celtic Park on September 10, 2016. (Photo by Steve Welsh/Getty Images)

"It feels great. To score a hat-trick, my first in professional football, is something unbelievable. Everyone has welcomed me since I came to the club, and the fans were unbelievable today.

"The atmosphere is something I have never seen. I don't think I will see something like this in my career. "

Final word for now goes to the Celtic captain, Scott Brown. He had remained silent whilst Joey Barton, brought in from English Championship side Burnley on a reputedly large salary, had bad-mouthed him in the media, claiming that Brown was "nowhere near the level of player I am."

The controversial midfielder's words had come back to haunt him, the veteran Celt dominating proceedings from the outset, leaving the field to a standing ovation on 74 minutes, the game and Joey already in the bag.

Pressed by the headline-seeking media afterwards about the anticipated "Battle with Barton," Brown dismissed it out of hand.

Brendan Rodgers coach of Celtic shakes hands with captain Scott Brown during the Scottish Premier league match between Celtic and Rangers at Celtic Park on September 10, 2016. (Photo by Jeff J Mitchell/Getty Images)

"It was easy. There was no battling whatsoever. It was pretty much men versus boys at the end of the day."

Invincible by Matt Corr. Photo via Celtistarbooks.com

articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks' 13-10 win over the New England Patriots on Wednesday night came with much significance.

The win marked the 11th-straight victory for the Seahawks , dating back to Nov. 16 of last year. This has tied their longest win streak in franchise history, which was set during the 2005 season. Seattle has been on a tear since that time, having won the Super Bowl at the end of last season and now started the 2026 NFL season off on the right foot.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba was the top performer for the Seahawks in the win over New England . JSN torched the Patriots for 122 receiving yards and a receiving touchdown in the win. This was the first time that he has ever recorded a touchdown in a Week 1 game in his career.

Josh Jobe delivered for Seattle in the biggest moment. He caught the game-sealing interception at the end of the game to give the Seahawks the victory. Jobe allowed two receptions for three receiving yards when targeted three times in coverage, according to NFL Next Gen Stats (via The 33rd Team), which highlighted the scope of his effect on the game.

The Seahawks put together a big win over the Patriots that starts them off on the right foot for the year.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Reveals He’s Reconciled with Brother Jordan Rodgers After Years of Estrangement
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback spoke at length about his family during a recent podcast appearance
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers is opening up about his recent family reunion following a years-long estrangement.

Appearing on the Not Just Football podcast with Pittsburgh Steelers teammate Cam Heyward on Thursday, Sept. 10, the 42-year-old quarterback spoke about reconnecting with his parents and siblings, a moment he chronicled on Instagram earlier this summer. Rodgers also revealed that he's reconciled with his younger brother Jordan Rodgers , who was not in the photos.

"There's been a few things that have happened the last couple of years, which has made the idea of reconciling with my parents first an opportunity," Aaron said in the Thursday, Sept. 10 episode, noting how his parents, Ed and Darla Rodgers, planned to relocate to Nashville from Chico, Calif., where the quarterback was raised.

"... The last day they were in Chico, was the day I met them there at their house, the house I bought them and built for them. And so, full circle. A couple weeks after that, went out to Nashville, met up with my older brother [Luke Rodgers], and a couple weeks after that, met up with my little brother [Jordan Rodgers]," the future Hall of Famer continued. "It was cool. There were tough conversations for sure, but I'm just in a much better headspace."

Rodgers stunned fans in July when he posted a collection of heartfelt images featuring his parents and older brother Luke. "Another bonding week," the future Hall of Famer captioned the post .

The Super Bowl-winning quarterback had long been estranged from his family, with the feud coming into public view in 2016 when Jordan appeared on JoJo Fletcher 's season of The Bachelorette . Jordan claimed on the show that he and Aaron "don't really have that much of a relationship."

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

"Nobody knew anything that was going on with it," Aaron said on Thursday's podcast episode. "I decided I didn't want to play this out in the media because I didn't think that was right. Now, other members of my family would say things, whether the intent was to harm, a couple times it was by a few of them, a couple times they really didn't know what was going on. They didn't know what it would be like to have a son who was super-famous. I didn't know what it would be like after the Super Bowl, to be super-famous in the way that I was, and how that changes relationships and the relationships dissolved. Now, full circle, they're back together. It's amazing. It's been great to have all those people, my little brother, my older brother and his family, my parents, that's been really, really special."

Aaron credited his wife , Brittani, for helping mend the fences.

"My wife deserves a lot of the credit for that just to be able to get to that point to think about having the conversations, she was a big part of that," he said Thursday. "And not that she was pushing anything, she wasn't, it was more, and you guys can probably relate to this, when you're loved by someone in such an unconditional, beautiful, pure way, it changes your perspective on all of your relationships around that. That becomes your anchor point. Well, if I can be made to feel like this by this person, I feel like it opens up your heart in an even deeper way that I never experienced before. A year ago, even two years ago, five years ago for sure, I would have said, 'Nah, I'm never going to reconcile.'"

Aaron, who is suiting up for what is expected to be his final NFL season, said his dad previously "came up to" a Steelers game. "Hopefully, we'll get them all out," he said Thursday. "Was just talking with my brother, my little brother's birthday was yesterday and he was just in Ireland calling a game."

Before posting the photos on Instagram, Aaron publicly reunited with his family in April. In a photo obtained by PEOPLE, Aaron sat with his parents at the Pleasant Valley High School banquet dinner in Chico, Calif., as he celebrated his induction into his high school's athletics hall of fame.

A four-time league MVP, Aaron is playing in his 22nd NFL season and his second with the Steelers. He spent the first 18 years of his career in Green Bay, winning a Super Bowl in February 2010. Aaron was then traded to the Jets in 2023 and spent two years in New York.

The Steelers host the Indianapolis Colts in their season opener on Sunday, Sept. 13.

articles.title: Across the US, high school sports provide a sense of community — and, for some, a way out
articles.summary: “When will the senior citizen passes be available?” Aliquippa High athletic director Jennifer Damico’s office heard more than once as the latest season of Qu...
articles.body:
The phone calls started coming long before the lights at "The Pit" flickered on for the first time this fall.

"When will the senior citizen passes be available?" Aliquippa High athletic director Jennifer Damico's office heard more than once as the latest season of Quips football inched forward.

At the school about 30 minutes northwest of downtown Pittsburgh, the passes have been a longstanding tradition — a way for the community's past to connect with its present.

A lot has changed in the century-plus since Aliquippa first opened its doors. The Aliquippa Works steel mill, which employed well over 10,000 workers at its height before the industry collapsed, is long gone. Many storefronts in the heart of the borough's business district sit empty.

One of the few constants through the years has been those precious hours every week during the fall when the Quips storm out of the locker room.

"We might be going to different churches on Sunday at 11," says coach Mike Warfield, an Alquippa alum and retired state trooper who believes the program saved his life twice. "But on Fridays at 7, we're together."

Amid an ever-changing landscape, when a constant distraction sits in the palm of your hand, and the culture wars seem specifically designed to divide, those Friday nights and everything they represent endure.

"It may be overstated, but I think it's kind of an American institution," says Bruce Howard, director of publications and communications at the National Federation of State High School Associations director of publications and communications. "If you played on a sports team in school, you're still talking about it. You still remember it."

In a country in which nearly a third of the population tunes in to the Super Bowl, the confluence between sports and community may be felt most acutely in far smaller venues.

A tradition that is thriving across the board

A century-plus ago, organized sports at the local level were a mishmash. There were no real age limits or parameters. Around the dawn of the 20th century, state athletic associations began to pop up in the Midwest, hoping to establish a little order amid the chaos. The model they created provided the framework for what has become an intrinsic part of the high school experience.

Today, even with competition from youth travel leagues, prep sports are thriving. The NFHS's annual survey for the 2025-26 academic year estimated there were over 8.4 million participants in high school sports, a 25% jump since the 20th century became the 21st.

The expansion of opportunities — particularly on the girls' side with flag football and wrestling — has helped. It also looks good on a college resume.

Yet the roots, particularly for the 1.1 million high school football players and what they have come to represent, run far deeper than that.

The bond between players, school and community can be timeless

Rich Boronyak grew up in Crafton, Pennsylvania, 60 years ago. A three-sport star at long-since-closed Crafton High, he remembers the parade the town threw after a football championship. The faces that lined those streets are still so fresh in his mind.

"Everybody knew everybody," he said from the stands at "The Pit" while waiting for his grandson, who plays football for Mars Area High, to take on the Quips.

It remains that way in countless places across the nation, though perhaps few where the pressure and the privilege of playing are more intertwined than Aliquippa.

It's not just the record 21 regional championships, the five state titles, and the notable alumni like Pro Football Hall of Famers Mike Ditka, Ty Law and Darrelle Revis. It's all of it.

Senior running back Akiva Woods says "there's a huge standard to stay up to."

Reminders dot the stands at home games, where the alums reminisce and keep tabs on the latest members of what all involved universally describe as a family.

Things have changed since Paul Royba graduated in 1984. Back then, there was no pregame hype video. No cameras capturing every moment. Gone are the miserable grass field and the locker room where hot water was more myth than fact.

And still, part of the appeal remains eternal.

"The mentality and the spirit has stayed the same," says Royba, now 60 and recently retired after 34 years in the corporate world.

That spirit is described on Quips T-shirts: "Aliquippa against the world." The school of around 320 students does its best to silence the outside noise that their hometown is poor, small and dangerous.

"Athletics is what I believe has kept this place going," Damico says. "There's been good economic times and bad, but the athletics is always the constant, always the positive story that is coming out of here."

Things are hardly perfect, but they're hardly perfect anywhere.

America's harsh realities in 2026 have a way of showing up. About an hour east of the Quips and the Mars Planets game, longtime rivals Gateway and Penn Hills played in front of a mostly empty stadium after school officials learned of a "potential threat."

For some, the lights provide the launching pad for the American dream

For Woods, his goals lie beyond Aliquippa. He's already received scholarship offers from nearby Division II schools, and he's hoping a standout senior year turns even more heads.

It's working out that way for Lester Longmire. A year ago, he was a senior linebacker and one of the leaders of the defense. Now he's a special teamer and freshman sports management major at Slippery Rock University, about an hour north.

Standing on the sideline as the Quips struggled in the first half against Mars, Longmire talks about the urge to get away, even though it means leaving his support system and everyone he cares about.

"I do miss football. I miss the community and all that," he says. "But I want to start a new life, so I plan on staying out of here."

Just not quite yet. Eager to encourage his former teammates, Longmire wades into the sea of red-and-black jerseys.

As he walks away, the safety and the promise of the Friday night lights and all they have meant and all they will mean cradle him once more.

articles.title: Latest injury ups 49ers' need for former Georgia first-round pick
articles.summary: The 49ers need former Georgia first-round pick Mykel Williams to return from injury after defensive tackle Alfred Collins was ruled out for the season
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers already are dealing with injuries along their defensive front. 49ers defensive tackle Alfred Collins was expected to play a large role in his second season, but is now out of the season after suffering a torn patellar tendon just days before San Francisco 's season opener against the Los Angeles Rams on Sept. 10 in Australia.

As a rookie in 2025, Collins posted 17 tackles, a sack and forced a pair of fumbles. Collins is former second-round pick out of Texas.

Collins' injury puts more pressure on former Georgia Bulldogs first-round pick Mykel Williams to return to action. Williams suffered a torn ACL last season and is on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list to start the season. Williams will miss the 49ers first four games of the season.

Williams recorded 20 tackles and one sack in his rookie season (2025) with the 49ers. San Francisco needs him and the defensive front as a whole to be healthy. Coach Kyle Shanahan is hoping to get more production out of Williams in Year 2.

The 49ers will have to find a delicate balance of limiting Williams' snaps to preserve his health while still giving him enough playing time to develop into a defensive force. Williams can return for the 49ers Week 5 game against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks .

The 49ers open the season on Thursday, Sept. 10 at 8:35 p.m. ET against the Los Angeles Rams (televised on Netflix).
